brief: Goldman's desk roundup covers the week into the September FOMC. Research moves to a 25bp hike next week from a hold, not on the economics but on the mechanics: Warsh's Jackson Hole guidance took market pricing to nearly 90%, so the FOMC is expected to avoid the reaction a hold would bring. GS still sees no strong economic case, calls the decision less clear-cut than pricing implies, and keeps further hikes out of its baseline. August core CPI at 0.29% ran above expectations and lifts the August core PCE estimate to 0.26% from 0.24%. The same perceived high bar to tighten explains the Dollar's weak response to CPI, so next week's decision is the pivot for Dollar direction, with a delivered hike Dollar positive but risks skewed lower. The Yen is up over 4% in eight sessions and the desk wants tactical long JPY funded out of EUR rather than USD. Bonds sold off globally with no single driver, oil through $100 and a smaller than expected Treasury buyback drove an Asia rout, and year-end 2026 10y forecasts rise to 4.75% in the US and 3.25% in Germany. Prime flows show macro product shorting against TMT buying.
